label: early-position input of u/s/t/p/d/n
explanation: Update-gate coordinate that fires when one of the letters u, s, t, p, d, n (u and s strongest) is input in the first five steps of the sequence (t <= 4). 97% of the activation mass is in the original phase, and nothing fires at t >= 6. At t = 0 it fires on exactly these six tokens (precision 1.0). Later positions are weaker and less reliable, with an uneven positional profile: t=0 and t=3 are strongest, t=2 and t=4 are moderate, and t=1 is weak (precision 0.23). It is also somewhat more likely when none of the six tokens has appeared earlier (adding ~seen raises F1 only slightly, to 0.63). Its small copy-phase activity comes from short sequences where step 3-4 already falls after <DEL>. It is near-silent on the <DEL> step, on later copy steps, and on other tokens; digits and r/x/w/y/a fire only rarely. Dev F1 is about 0.60 and mass recall 0.82. The remaining false positives at t = 1..4 depend on context in ways I did not capture.
